decisions.title: CommandIdentity is the only per-command identity; IdempotencyContext is its only idempotency projection
decisions.decision: Every command entry projects exactly one acp_services.workspace.command_identity.CommandIdentity (from_verified_http for an authenticated HTTP/MCP caller, from_server for the Controller process, from_local only for the explicit local-single operator). The idempotency scope id is identity.idempotency_scope(project_id=...) = resolve_scope_id(principal, project) and IdempotencyContext carries that scope plus identity.principal_id/key_id. No entry may build a second scope, fold a permission scope into the key, or hard-code LOCAL_PRINCIPAL_ID for an authenticated caller.
decisions.rationale: Before M0-04 the HTTP submit entry hard-coded LOCAL_PRINCIPAL_ID while admission recorded the process default, so two authenticated users in one project shared one idempotency scope and one admission principal (a retry replayed the other user's task).
decisions.rollback: Server-side only, no wire change. Rollback = stop the Controller, restore the jobs DB snapshot taken before migration 024, and deploy the pre-M0-04 build; rows already written with identity_version=2 are not silently downgraded (the old code folds the principal and cannot find them), so idempotency_records must be archived with the rollback rather than rewritten in place.

vectors.asserts: an authenticated request yields that user's principal, never LOCAL_PRINCIPAL_ID
two users in one project with one key get conflict, not a replay
the admission ledger attributes each reservation to its own principal
the CLI local operator is an explicit CommandIdentity.from_local, scope included

decisions.notes: LOCAL_PRINCIPAL_ID stays legal on exactly one path: the explicit local-single operator.

decisions.title: v1 request fields are extra=forbid with one 422 rule vocabulary and an empty legacy allowlist
decisions.decision: acp_services.entrypoints.application_params is the single authority for what a v1 request field means. An undeclared execution field is refused with input_invalid/params.rule=unknown_field (HTTP 422); a server path is refused with input_invalid/params.rule=unsupported_server_path (HTTP 422). There is no 'ignore unknown and warn' mode. LEGACY_REQUEST_FIELD_ALLOWLIST is empty in v1 and a future row must carry removal_version + exit_condition (FieldPolicy rejects a row without them).
decisions.rationale: The v1 DTO silently dropped unknown fields, so a typo such as execution_mod degraded into a local run instead of an error. The mechanical client inventory (scripts/acceptance/check_v1_request_field_consumers.py) found no undeclared field in use, so v1 can hard-cut instead of carrying a permanent dual field policy.
decisions.rollback: Revert = add the field to SUBMIT_FIELD_POLICY and, only if a shipped client needs a transition window, add a legacy_allowlist row with removal_version + exit_condition. No DB change. Re-introducing a silent 'ignore unknown' mode is not a legal rollback: it was the defect U1 removes.

field_decision.preflight_field_set: identical to submit (one normalised body, two commands)

legacy_allowlist.exit_condition_rule: A future allowlist row must carry removal_version + exit_condition (FieldPolicy rejects a row without them), name the consumer set, and state the condition that proves no client sends the field any more (the same mechanical scanner must report that consumer as gone). The v1 allowlist is empty because every registered consumer sends declared fields only; there is deliberately no 'ignore unknown and warn' mode.
legacy_allowlist.inventory_basis: M0-06 manual inventory plus this task's mechanical scan: scripts/acceptance/check_v1_request_field_consumers.py

decisions.title: P2 implementation_status is the three-value enum planned|delivered|verified
decisions.decision: Every P2 row's implementation_status is exactly one of planned, delivered, verified. planned = promised but not callable (unregistered tools are refused as unknown_tool and acp_capabilities answers implemented=false); delivered = the registered tool set covers the row in code with contract-level evidence; verified = delivered plus live producer-to-consumer evidence. Advertising an extension never promotes a row: a partial implementation never reports negotiated=true (ADR-006 D7).
decisions.rationale: The audit found 'advertised' read as 'delivered'. One enum with an explicit verified level keeps the three-state evidence rule (PASS/FAIL/NOT_VERIFIED) aligned with the contract vocabulary.
decisions.rollback: None needed at runtime: the field is documentation of delivery state. Rolling a row back from delivered to planned is legal only with a contract change that also removes the tool registration; downgrading verified to delivered is legal and expected when live evidence expires.

vectors.asserts: the five P2 rows, owners and tool names are frozen
every P2 row carries exactly planned|delivered|verified

decisions.title: Planning claim namespace plan|<project>|<research>|<session>|<round>|<call_seq>
decisions.decision: A planning/model claim id is the pipe-joined tuple plan|<project>|<research>|<session>|<round>|<call_seq>. Every segment is non-empty, contains no '|', and is server-derived (the client supplies neither project nor research/session identity). call_seq is monotonically increasing per (project, research, session, round). The claim carries its request_digest and a model receipt namespace (D-IDENT-05). It is a planning reservation id, never a submit ledger key: it must not be written to idempotency_records (whose action is submit) and it must not be an empty claim_id that escapes the partial index.
decisions.pending_reason: No implementation exists in this checkout: there is no plan_claim/call_seq producer anywhere under src/ (grep for 'plan|', call_seq, claim_key returns nothing). Writing frozen would declare a convention delivered that has no code, no ledger and no vector.
decisions.consumer_task: M1-04c (planning reservation; M1-02 for the research/session/round identity)
decisions.rationale: Without a stable planning identity a model call cannot be charged before a proposal exists, and a retry cannot be reconciled to the call it repeats.

entries: planning model call (gateway → runtime research budget ledger)

decisions.rollback: No runtime surface exists yet, so rollback is 'do not implement'. Once M1-04c lands, the convention is additive: a new claim namespace is a new prefix with its own segments, never a re-interpretation of a stored claim id.

vectors.asserts: the namespace is recorded as a forward convention with no producer in src/

decisions.notes: Exit condition: M1-04c implements the producer, a test pins the segment grammar, then this decision flips to frozen with a new commit.

decisions.title: Model receipt namespace modelrcpt|... binds research/round/call/request, never a job/attempt
decisions.decision: A model receipt id is modelrcpt|<project>|<research>|<session>|<round>|<call_seq>|<request_digest>. It is the settlement key for one model call, bound to research/round/call/request/model and explicitly NOT to a job_id or attempt (a model call is not a platform task). Unknown, stream-interrupted or unknown-outcome calls stay reserved and reconcile; a scientific rejection deletes no already-incurred model usage.
decisions.pending_reason: No model receipt producer exists under src/ (no 'modelrcpt', model_receipt or receipt_id producer for planning calls); the only receipt chain implemented today is the job-attempt receipt (runtime/receipt_identity.py), which is a different identity.
decisions.consumer_task: M1-04c (model settlement); M1-02 for the research round that owns the receipt
decisions.rationale: A receipt that binds to a job/attempt would be a false execution fact: planning happens before any task exists, and a rejected proposal still consumed model budget.

entries: model gateway → runtime research budget settlement

decisions.rollback: No runtime surface exists yet. Once implemented, receipt ids are persisted settlement facts: a rollback must not rewrite an existing receipt id, only stop producing new ones.

vectors.asserts: the receipt namespace is forward-only and carries no job/attempt segment

decisions.notes: Exit condition: M1-04c lands the producer + a settlement idempotency test, then this decision flips to frozen.

decisions.title: RPH research keys encode project/research/round with colon-joined segments; the platform treats them as opaque
decisions.decision: RPH derives its stable keys locally and the platform treats them as opaque. Current frozen encoding: researchRoundKey = '<project_id>:record:<research_id>:round-<round>'; researchEventKey = researchRoundKey + ':event:<eventId>'; the store indexes '<project_id>:record:<recordId>' and '<project_id>:proposal:<proposalId>'; the record id is '<research_id>:round-<round>'. project_id is always the first segment, round is always 'round-<n>', and segments never contain ':'. Change rule: a new segment is appended at the end behind a new key function; changing or reordering an existing segment requires a new key function plus a migration, because the value is persisted and replayed as an idempotency key.
decisions.rationale: The round key is the client-side idempotency key: a replay must address the same resource and a changed body must be duplicate_round, not a second record.
decisions.rollback: Keys live in the RPH client and in the platform's opaque idempotency ledger. A rollback of the key grammar keeps both key functions available and re-derives the old key for lookup; it never rewrites a stored client key.

decisions.title: plan_digest is a required segment of the RPH-derived stable key (forward, not implemented)
decisions.decision: When RPH derives a submit idempotency key for a research round it must bind project + research + round + plan_digest (the approved plan), persist the derived key before the call, and never rewrite it when the plan changes: a changed plan_digest invalidates the old approval and opens a new round/revision with a new key. Today RPH does not include plan_digest in any key and the bridge forwards a caller-supplied key.
decisions.pending_reason: The plan_digest segment has no producer: researchRoundKey/researchEventKey contain no plan_digest, and the bridge forwards request.idempotencyKey unchanged. Freezing it would document a key shape no code emits.
decisions.consumer_task: M1-02 (research submit intent persisted before the call; plan_digest invalidation)
decisions.rationale: Without plan_digest in the key, a revised plan could replay the previous intent's key and silently reuse an approval for different science.
decisions.rollback: Additive: a new key function appends the plan_digest segment; the old key stays for lookup of already-persisted intents.

vectors.asserts: the missing plan_digest segment is recorded as pending, not frozen

decisions.notes: Exit condition: M1-02 lands the derived key + a changed-plan test, then this decision flips to frozen.

decisions.title: Request digest rule v2 over the canonical request; v1 rows verified by their own frozen field table
decisions.decision: REQUEST_DIGEST_VERSION='2' hashes the field-policy canonical request (canonical_submit_request: exhaustive policy set, defaults materialised, node_tags normalised, server-path fields rejected before identity, schema_version always included). LEGACY_REQUEST_DIGEST_FIELDS freezes the v1 declaration (it still carries output_dir/config_path). A row written under another version is never called tampered: equal digest bytes mean the same request; otherwise the stored digest is re-derived from the row's own frozen field table, and an unverifiable difference is a typed conflict whose remedy is reconcile, never a blind resubmit with a new key.
decisions.rationale: Each entry used to hash whatever it happened to serialise, so the same logical request could be a different request per entry and a rule change looked like tampering.
decisions.rollback: A bump is additive: add the new field table to DIGEST_FIELD_TABLES before changing the constant. Rolling back to v1 without a table entry would make v2 rows unverifiable; the ledger then answers reconcile for those rows, which is safe but noisy, so a rollback keeps both tables registered.

vectors.asserts: v1 and v2 rules agree on a request that predates the policy
a v1 row replays on equal bytes and reconciles (never 'tampered') otherwise
a changed accepted field changes the digest and is a conflict

decisions.notes: digest fields are key-sorted, sequences keep order, floats are rendered as exact decimal strings (no JSON float).

decisions.title: Legacy auto_ derived keys are lookup-only; op_ is an operation reference and never a ledger key
decisions.decision: The pre-M0-05 MCP derivation auto_<sha256[:32]> (LEGACY_DERIVED_KEY_VERSION='auto-v1') is recomputed only to find a pre-existing local-single row; it is never applied to a client-supplied key and never claims a new row for an authenticated binding. op_<uuid> is the operation-reference namespace (prepare operation ids) and must never be written to the idempotency ledger as a key. A missing client key is explicitly non-idempotent; the adapter owns no result cache and no second ledger.
decisions.rationale: M0-05 removed the permission-scope fold: the old adapter folded scope+payload into an op_-looking key, so the ledger key was neither the client's nor attributable.
decisions.rollback: The derivation formula is byte-frozen so old rows stay findable; changing it would orphan them. Rolling back to a scope-folded key is not legal: it re-creates the unattributable rows R09 reconciles.

vectors.asserts: the ledger key is the raw client key; no op_ key is ever written
an auto_ row replays only on the local-single binding that wrote it
auto_ is a separate reconciliation namespace, not a second ledger

decisions.notes: An authenticated binding never claims the auto_ namespace.

decisions.title: Prepare surface conflict: MCP acp_prepare_artifact resource_id is not a prepare field
decisions.decision: Recorded, not resolved here: the RPH bridge requires resource_id for the prepare operation (OPERATION_FIELDS.prepare = task, attempt, resource) and the frozen bridge test asserts {job_id, attempt, resource_id}; the MCP tool schema declares resource_id; but PREPARE_FIELD_POLICY / V1PrepareRequest do not declare it, and since M0-06 services_mcp_bootstrap._ControllerArtifacts.prepare validates the raw MCP arguments against that policy, a prepare call that carries resource_id is rejected as input_invalid/unknown_field. The registered contract's prepare field list is also stale in the other direction (it lacks job_id/relative_path/expected_*/schema_ref/source_refs/evidence_report/media_type and declares extensions, which the policy does not). One owner must choose: add resource_id (and extensions?) to the prepare contract/DTO, or rename the bridge argument to artifact_id.
decisions.pending_reason: Two frozen surfaces disagree and choosing one is a contract change, not a freeze: the scan proves the client is rejected today (breaking: rph:buildToolArguments:prepare, contract_divergence: acceptance prepare bodies).
decisions.rationale: A prepare path that answers 422 for its own documented argument is a live regression of the v1 field cut, so it must be named before M1-01 freezes the artifact contract.
decisions.rollback: Nothing was changed, so there is nothing to roll back; the resolution (M1-01) must either widen the prepare field policy (a v1.3 additive field) or rename the bridge argument, and either choice carries its own vector.
